title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, organizes, analyzes, and presents data to answer business or research questions. Applied Statistics & Analytics provides a strong foundation for this career because it emphasizes probability, statistical inference, sampling, regression, and quantitative reasoning.

about.label: Career level
about.text: Data Analytics Intern → Junior Data Analyst → Data Analyst → Senior Analyst

about.label: Core industries
about.text: Banking, healthcare, retail, consulting, technology, manufacturing, logistics, education

about.label: Primary objective
about.text: Transform raw data into reliable insights that help organizations understand performance, identify trends, investigate problems, and make evidence-based decisions

sections.heading: What does a Data Analyst do?

blocks.text: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, organizes, analyzes, and presents data to answer business or research questions. Applied Statistics & Analytics provides a strong foundation for this career because it emphasizes probability, statistical inference, sampling, regression, and quantitative reasoning.

For example, an e-commerce company may want to understand why sales declined in a particular month. A Data Analyst could combine sales and marketing data, identify changes across products and customer segments, visualize the trends, and recommend areas for further investigation.
Core responsibilities

items.text: Collect data from spreadsheets, databases, business applications, surveys, and other sources.
Clean missing, duplicated, inconsistent, or incorrectly formatted records.
Use SQL and spreadsheets to filter, join, aggregate, and summarize data.
Apply descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, correlation, and regression where appropriate.
Identify trends, anomalies, relationships, and changes in key performance indicators.
Build dashboards and reports using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
Communicate findings through charts, written summaries, and presentations.
Validate data quality, definitions, calculations, and reporting assumptions.
Work with stakeholders to define business questions and analytical requirements.
Maintain reproducible queries, documentation, and regular reporting workflows.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: A Data Analyst focuses on understanding and communicating what the data shows and why patterns may have occurred. A Data Scientist often undertakes more advanced predictive modeling and experimentation, while a Data Engineer concentrates on building and maintaining data pipelines and infrastructure. The boundaries vary by organization.

rows.text: Excel, SQL, data cleaning, basic statistics
Independent analysis, KPI tracking, stakeholder insights
Analytics Manager / BI Lead / Analytics Specialist
Team leadership, reporting strategy, organizational decision support

blocks.text: Progression depends on analytical ability, business understanding, communication, and the complexity of the projects handled.
This plan assumes a three-year B.Sc. program. If your university offers a four-year degree, use the additional year for advanced statistics, research, internships, or a major analytics project.
Year 1
Foundation
Build mathematical and data fundamentals

items.text: Study descriptive statistics, probability, calculus fundamentals, and linear algebra.
Learn Excel formulas, lookup functions, pivot tables, charts, and data cleaning.
Learn Python fundamentals, NumPy, pandas, and basic visualization.
Understand data types, sampling, distributions, averages, variability, and outliers.
Practise writing clear analytical summaries and presenting numerical findings.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Analyze a public dataset on education, retail sales, transport, or public health. Clean the data, calculate summary statistics, and create a visual report.

blocks.label: Expected outcome
blocks.text: Work with structured data and explain basic statistical findings accurately.
Year 2
Core analytics
Develop statistical analysis and database skills

items.text: Study sampling distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, correlation, and regression.
Learn SQL queries, joins, grouping, subqueries, and common table expressions.
Practise data transformation, exploratory data analysis, and feature creation.
Learn Power BI or Tableau for dashboards, calculated measures, and interactive reporting.
Understand data quality checks, selection bias, confounding, and the difference between correlation and causation.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Analyze customer, sales, or operational data to identify trends and investigate a specific business question.

blocks.label: Industry exposure
blocks.text: Seek internships in data analytics, business intelligence, market research, or statistical analysis.
Year 3
Job readiness
Deliver end-to-end analytical projects

items.text: Apply regression, statistical testing, segmentation, and time-series fundamentals where appropriate.
Build dashboards that answer defined stakeholder questions.
Automate recurring data preparation and reporting with SQL or Python.
Learn basic data modeling, KPI definitions, and business requirements gathering.
Document analytical assumptions, limitations, and recommendations.
Practise SQL interviews, case studies, statistical reasoning, and presentation skills.

blocks.label: Capstone
blocks.text: Analyze a multi-table dataset, build a reproducible SQL/Python workflow, create an interactive dashboard, and present recommendations supported by evidence.

blocks.label: Expected outcome
blocks.text: Demonstrate a complete workflow from raw data to a clear, decision-oriented report.

rows.text: Excel, pivot tables, lookups, Power Query
KPIs, growth rates, conversion, retention, margins
A/B testing fundamentals, bias, causal limitations
Time-series patterns, moving averages, forecast evaluation
Tables, relationships, measures, dimensional modeling basics

blocks.text: Because the degree emphasizes applied statistics, use that advantage: a good analyst does not merely produce charts but understands uncertainty, sampling limitations, and whether the evidence supports a conclusion.
Build three or four projects that demonstrate statistical reasoning, practical analysis, and clear communication.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Sales performance analysis
Beginner
Analyze sales by product, region, month, and customer segment. Identify growth patterns, underperforming categories, and possible seasonal effects.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Clean dataset, Excel workbook, charts, and an executive summary.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Excel, descriptive statistics, data cleaning, visualization.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Business intelligence dashboard
Intermediate
Build an interactive dashboard for sales, customer retention, inventory, or operations. Define each KPI clearly and allow users to filter by date, category, or region.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Power BI dashboard, data model, metric definitions, and a short user guide.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: SQL, Power BI, data modeling, business metrics.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Statistical investigation
Intermediate

Investigate a specific question, such as whether customer satisfaction differs between groups or whether a measured factor is associated with an outcome. Select an appropriate statistical method and state the assumptions.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Analysis notebook, test results, visualizations, interpretation, and limitations.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Probability, hypothesis testing, regression, Python or R.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Demand or sales forecasting
Advanced
Analyze time-based data, establish a baseline forecast, and compare suitable forecasting methods using a time-ordered validation strategy.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Forecasting notebook, error metrics, forecast visualization, and a discussion of uncertainty.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Time-series analysis, Python, forecasting, model evaluation.

For every project, include the question being investigated, the dataset source, data-cleaning decisions, methods used, results, limitations, and practical recommendations. Never imply that an association proves causation without suitable evidence.

blocks.text: Illustrative employers to research include TCS, Infosys, Accenture, Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and analytics teams within banks, retailers, healthcare companies, and technology businesses. These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current openings.

blocks.label: Search terms
blocks.text: Data Analyst Intern, Junior Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Intern, Statistical Analyst, Research Analyst, and Reporting Analyst.
For entry-level applications, prioritize job descriptions that match your actual skills. A strong combination of SQL, Excel, Power BI, and applied statistics is a practical starting point.

Optional certificates in data analytics or business intelligence can help structure your learning. Before paying, verify the current syllabus, assessment, cost, and employer recognition. A certificate should complement—not replace—projects that demonstrate analytical ability.
Further study is optional for many entry-level Data Analyst positions. It may help if you want to specialize in advanced statistics, research, economics, or data science.

rows.text: Healthcare, clinical research, public health data

blocks.text: For roles involving statistical research or advanced quantitative modeling, a postgraduate degree can be particularly useful. Check program-specific eligibility and prerequisites before applying.

blocks.label: AI-assisted analytics
blocks.text: Tools can help draft queries, summarize findings, and generate visualizations, but outputs need verification.

blocks.label: Automated data quality checks
blocks.text: Validation rules help detect missing values, duplicates, and unexpected changes.

blocks.label: Cloud analytics platforms
blocks.text: Managed data warehouses and analytics services support larger, more collaborative workflows.

blocks.label: Semantic data models
blocks.text: Standardized metric definitions improve consistency across dashboards and teams.

blocks.label: Causal inference and experimentation
blocks.text: Better methods help distinguish genuine effects from correlations and confounding.

blocks.label: Natural-language querying
blocks.text: Users can ask questions in plain language, while analysts remain responsible for validating the generated queries and interpretations.

blocks.label: Privacy-aware analytics
blocks.text: Data minimization, access control, and responsible handling of sensitive information are increasingly important.
The durable advantage is statistical judgment: knowing which question to ask, which method to use, and what conclusions the available data can actually support.
Data Analyst readiness
Clean and transform a dataset using Excel or Python
Write SQL queries using joins, grouping, and aggregations
Explain probability, distributions, and sampling
Perform hypothesis tests and interpret confidence intervals
Build a clear and interactive Power BI or Tableau dashboard
Define KPIs and validate calculations
Explain the difference between correlation and causation
Complete at least two documented analytics projects
Present findings and recommendations to a non-technical audience
Document data sources, assumptions, and analytical limitations
Reset checklist
By graduation, aim to present yourself as a statistics-focused Data Analyst who can query, clean, analyze, visualize, and interpret data to solve practical problems.
Prioritize five capabilities:

blocks.label: Statistics
blocks.text: Understand uncertainty, sampling, inference, and regression.

Your strongest entry-level positioning is: “I can turn raw data into reliable insights by combining statistical reasoning, SQL, Python, and business intelligence tools.”
